svg.text: A 2-way set-associative cache at work: miss, hit, conflict, eviction
A small version of Sixfold's caches (4 sets instead of 64). Address = tag | set (2 bits) | offset (5 bits): each line holds 32 bytes.

g.text: 1. The set bits pick set 2 in BOTH ways (highlighted).
2. Two comparators check both stored tags against 0x40 at the same time.
The pipeline waits 11 cycles while the refill engine
fetches the 32-byte line. It goes into an empty way.
LRU now points at way 1. Next-line prefetch starts.
1. The set bits pick set 2 in BOTH ways (highlighted).
2. Two comparators check both stored tags against 0x40 at the same time.
The data comes back this same cycle: 0 extra cycles.
LRU for set 2 now points at way 1
(the way NOT just used is next to go).
1. The set bits pick set 2 in BOTH ways (highlighted).
2. Two comparators check both stored tags against 0x50 at the same time.
The pipeline waits 11 cycles while the refill engine
fetches the 32-byte line. It goes into an empty way.
LRU now points at way 0. Next-line prefetch starts.
1. The set bits pick set 2 in BOTH ways (highlighted).
2. Two comparators check both stored tags against 0x60 at the same time.
The pipeline waits 11 cycles while the refill engine
fetches the 32-byte line. It goes into way 0, the least recently used.
LRU now points at way 1. Next-line prefetch starts.
1. The set bits pick set 2 in BOTH ways (highlighted).
2. Two comparators check both stored tags against 0x50 at the same time.
The data comes back this same cycle: 0 extra cycles.
LRU for set 2 now points at way 0
(the way NOT just used is next to go).

svg.text: Why two ways? 0x2040 and 0x2840 share set 2. A direct-mapped cache would throw one out every time; here both fit,
until a third line of set 2 (0x3040) arrives and replaces the one used longest ago.
Same behaviour as src/Data_Cache.sv and src/Instruction_Cache.sv (64 sets there); drawn by tools/animations.mjs.
